title: How Do LLM-Generated Texts Impact Term-Based Retrieval Models?
abstract: arXiv:2508.17715v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: As more content generated by large language models (LLMs) floods into the Internet, information retrieval (IR) systems now face the challenge of distinguishing and handling a blend of human-authored and machine-generated texts. Recent studies suggest that neural retrievers may exhibit a preferential inclination toward LLM-generated content, while classic term-based retrievers like BM25 tend to favor human-written documents. This paper investigates the influence of LLM-generated content on term-based retrieval models, which are valued for their efficiency and robust generalization across domains. Our linguistic analysis reveals that LLM-generated texts exhibit smoother high-frequency and steeper low-frequency Zipf slopes, higher term specificity, and greater document-level diversity. These traits are aligned with LLMs being trained to optimize reader experience through diverse and precise expressions. Our study further explores

translated_title: 大语言模型生成的文本如何影响基于词项的检索模型？
translated_abstract: arXiv:2508.17715v2 公告类型：replace-cross 摘要：随着越来越多由大语言模型（LLM）生成的内容涌入互联网，信息检索（IR）系统如今面临着区分和处理人类撰写与机器生成文本混合内容的挑战。近期研究表明，神经检索器可能对LLM生成的内容表现出偏好性倾向，而像BM25这样的经典基于词项的检索器则更倾向于人类撰写的文档。本文研究了LLM生成的内容对基于词项的检索模型的影响，这类模型因其高效性和跨领域的强泛化能力而备受重视。我们的语言学分析揭示，LLM生成的文本呈现出更平缓的高频段和更陡峭的低频段Zipf斜率、更高的词项特异性以及更大的文档级多样性。这些特征与LLM被训练为通过多样且精确的表达来优化读者体验相一致。我们的研究进一步探讨了……
tldr: 本文通过语言学分析发现LLM生成的文本具有独特的词频分布、更高的词项特异性和文档多样性，并据此研究了这些特征如何影响以BM25为代表的基于词项的检索模型的表现。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through linguistic analysis that LLM-generated texts exhibit distinctive Zipf slopes, higher term specificity, and greater document-level diversity, and investigates how these characteristics influence term-based retrieval models such as BM25.
